_doc: M13, the fall (docs/17). Where the sixteen land, what the lead is told on landing, the standing quest every lead carries, and how the others live their own lives. Read by src/chronicle/fall.gd and src/chronicle/wanderers.gd. Everything marked Inferred in docs/17 is a default the build took so it could keep moving; it is agenda items 25 to 29 in docs/worldbuilding/answers.md.

crash._doc: A crash site is any open, walkable ground joined by land to the Tower, never on a place, and drawn from the world seed rather than from the world's dice. The lead's crash site becomes the company's Home (agenda item 15).
crash._doc_first_world: D101: in the first world (no world has ended before it) the lead comes down on the road to the great city, between city_min and city_max tiles from it, so the First Hour reaches the Tower's city in minutes. min_tower_distance and max_haven_distance do not apply there; the rest do. Later worlds keep the far rule. The road's length is **Inferred** (12 to 14 against 18 to 20, open since meeting 2) and is settled after doug-md plays it.

landing._doc: The beat played the first time the world opens on a new run. {name} is the lead, {region} where they landed, {ground} the land under them (data/biomes.json), {tower_way} which way the Tower stands from there, {city} the great city and {city_way} which way it lies. A line with `lead` is said only when that one of the sixteen is the lead. D101: Sky comes down in the crater with Atlas, and Bram pulls the lead out; the flash of the sixteen's ring is the meeting 2 beat. A line with `unless` is not said for the leads it names: Cato and the leads with a chapter one (D135, D138) answer Bram in their own words in place of the shared last line, so his crater stays at five boxes with the sibling world's line. D122 (meeting 4): at most five boxes before the first step, so five lines for Atlas and four for anyone else; the journal and the standing quest go to the log (`note`).

lines.text: Something tears across the sky and comes down in {region}. When the smoke thins there is a crater ploughed into the {ground}, and {name} wakes at the bottom of it with no memory of falling. For a heartbeat there is a ring of sixteen lights behind the eyes. Then it is gone.
Something else came down with {name}: a great lizard, too heavy for its own legs, already pushing its head under {name}'s hand. Its name comes back before anything else does. Sky.

lines.speaker: Bram
lines.text: Easy. Easy, now. Give me your hand. I saw you come down, and I didn't think there'd be anybody left to pull out.

lines.speaker: Bram
lines.text: That's the Tower, off to the {tower_way}, and {city} at the foot of it, to the {city_way}. The Guild's there. Nobody goes up that thing without the Guild's say-so.

lines.speaker: {name}
lines.text: Up. Whatever I was, it was up there. I am going back.

lines.speaker: {name}
lines.text: Good. Somebody up there kept rules. I'll learn theirs.

lines.speaker: {name}
lines.text: A tower nobody is allowed to climb. Mm. That is the first interesting thing anyone has said to me.

lines.speaker: {name}
lines.text: Then the Guild is the chain of command here. Good. I'll know where I stand by nightfall.

lines.speaker: {name}
lines.text: And who decided the Guild gets the say-so? I'll ask them. Then I'll climb it anyway.

lines.speaker: {name}
lines.text: Then I will ask the Guild kindly. And if they say no, I will ask them why.

lines.speaker: {name}
lines.text: The Guild's mark. Fine. I've started at the bottom before.

lines.speaker: {name}
lines.text: I don't need anybody's say-so. I'm looking for someone. If they went up it, so will I.

lines.speaker: {name}
lines.text: Say-so? Ha! I'll climb it, and they can tell me off at the top.

lines.speaker: {name}
lines.text: HA! Then I'll go and get their say-so, and then I'll go up it.

lines.speaker: {name}
lines.text: Then I'll get their say-so! Where do I sign? You'll hear them cheer for me yet.

lines.speaker: {name}
lines.text: Everyone always wants up. I'll climb it. I'm not promising to stay up there.

lines.speaker: {name}
lines.text: The Guild! Then everyone who's anyone goes through there. Perfect. Who else did you pull out?

lines.speaker: {name}
lines.text: Say-so can wait. Has anybody here eaten today? You look like you haven't.

lines.speaker: {name}
lines.text: Then the Guild had better have a kitchen. Come on, I'll cook while you tell me who else came down.

lines.speaker: {name}
lines.text: Can I go round it? The city, I mean. There are a lot of people.

landing.note: A journal came down too, blank but for the name on its first page. A new standing quest: Ascend to heaven.

standing_quest._doc: D53: every lead carries one standing quest from landing. It never completes until the contest past the top is built (M17).
standing_quest.title: Ascend to heaven
standing_quest.brief: You fell from somewhere above, and the fall took everything you knew. The Tower is the only road up. Climb it.
standing_quest.not_started: Not a foot on the Tower's stair yet.
standing_quest.sealed: The stair is sealed until the world is answered.
standing_quest.topped: The top has been reached. What waits past it is not yet known.

siblings._doc: M15, sixteen worlds (docs/17, D32, D33, D52). When a lead dies and ascends, their world ends and the next lead starts in a sibling world. Read by src/chronicle/siblings.gd. Everything here is a default the build took, Inferred: agenda items 50 to 55 in docs/worldbuilding/answers.md.
siblings._doc_perturbation: A sibling world is built on the first fallen world's seed, so the ground, the places and their names, and where each of the sixteen comes down, are the same. Then this share of what the world's dice dealt is dealt again: which gates are already open, and which books sit on which library's shelves. The world's own dice (bands, the roadside, upkeep) run from a new seed. 0 is an identical twin; 1 redeals every gate and shelf (agenda item 50).
siblings._doc_echo: D52: an earlier lead is alive in the later world as an ordinary person, the copy of them that never fell, with the personality they started with. They wait at the settlement nearest where the new lead fell for stay_steps before walking on by temper, and word of them is in the company's ears from the landing (agenda item 51).
siblings._doc_weapon: D33: the dead lead's signature weapon crash-lands in the next world, but not before the new lead has got as far as the old one: at least the old lead's level, and at least as high up the Tower (agenda item 52). Where it lands (agenda item 12): with anywhere, D60, `doug-md`'s answer, it is any open ground the company can walk to at least min_distance from where the new lead fell, and the rumour says which way. Without anywhere it falls back to open ground between min_distance and max_distance tiles off.
siblings._doc_ghost: D33: the dead lead's ghost is at the campfire once their news has arrived (the same moment the weapon lands). They share the journal of the run they died in a page at a time: an Outward temper opens with `outward` pages, an Inward one with `inward`, and every night at the fire adds `per_visit`. Finding their weapon opens the rest (agenda item 54).
siblings._doc_signatures: Every one of the sixteen has a weapon made for them (equipment.json, `signature`, suited to nobody). Until the sixteen are written the twelve stand-ins carry these (agenda item 55).

lines._doc: {name} is the dead lead, {lead} the living one, {weapon} the signature weapon, {way} a compass direction, {place} a place, {level} and {floor} how far the dead lead got.
lines.ending_sub: They were the one who was supposed to save it. It never comes back.
lines.landing: There is talk already, in {place}, of somebody called {name}. You have never met them. The name sits in your chest like a stone.
lines.weapon_lands: Something falls out of a clear sky far to the {way}, trailing fire, and the ground shakes. The company stops talking for a while.
lines.weapon_annal: {weapon}, made for {name} in another world, fell from the sky.
lines.weapon_rumour: A crater opened to the {way} of {place}, they say, near where you yourself came down, with a weapon standing up out of it. Nobody who has tried to swing it could make it behave.
lines.weapon_found: In the crater lies {weapon}, made for {name}, who died in another world. It is heavy in your hands in a way that has nothing to do with weight.
lines.weapon_found_annal: The company dug {weapon} out of its crater. It was made for {name}.
lines.echo_seen: Something about {name} catches in your throat. Somewhere else, they died. Here, they never fell.

echo_answer.NT: No. I would remember; I remember everything since the crater. You are looking at me as if I owed you something. I do not, yet.
echo_answer.NF: I think so. Not here. You look at me the way people look at graves. Whoever you lost, I am sorry.
echo_answer.SJ: No, and I would thank you not to stare. If I have done something, tell me plainly.
echo_answer.SP: Ha. Everyone says that. I've got one of those faces. Buy me a drink and we can pretend.

lines.ghost_first: The fire gutters, and {name} is sitting across it, the way they sat in the world that ended. You can see the logs through them.
lines.ghost_again: {name} is at the fire again, or never left it.
lines.ghost_ask_found: What did you find out there?
lines.ghost_floor_none: I never set foot on the Tower's stair.
lines.ghost_floor: Floor {floor} of the Tower was as high as I got.
lines.ghost_killer: {killer} put me down, and the world went with me.
lines.ghost_killer_none: I do not remember the end. Only the sky going out.
lines.ghost_well_none: Well? I walked, and then I stopped. Do better.
lines.ghost_found_none: Nothing I can give you yet.
lines.ghost_withheld: There is more. I do not know you well enough to give it all to you.
lines.ghost_opened: You found my weapon. Then you have earned all of it.
lines.ghost_weapon_landed: It came down to the {way} of where you fell. Go and get it before somebody else does.
lines.ghost_weapon_found: You are carrying it. Nobody will ever hold it right. Hold it anyway.
lines.ghost_weapon_waiting: Still falling. It will come down when you have got as far as I did.

wanderers._doc: The other leads, living their own lives (docs/17). Who they are is every hero in data/heroes.json that the run did not start with. Their temper is Inferred (heroes.json has none until the sixteen are written). They move between places by temper: `preferences` weights each kind of place by temper group (NT, NF, SJ, SP).
wanderers._doc_rules: Steps are the build's clock until M18. A wanderer stays at a place for stay_min..stay_max steps, then walks to the next at steps_per_tile. Nearer places are favoured by nearness (a place twice as far is half as likely). An Inward temper needs to have been met meetings_to_join times before they will walk with you; an Outward one, fewer. Each of the sixteen also has a place of their own (heroes.json `found_at`, from docs/21's "when someone else is the lead"): they walk there first, like that kind of place home_liking more than their temper does, and stay there home_stay times as long. A `restless` one (Iris, Liber) stays restless_stay as long anywhere. **Inferred** (docs/worldbuilding/answers.md).

lines._doc: What they say when met. {name} is the wanderer, {title} their title, {place} where you are both standing, {next} the kind of place they mean to go next, {lead} the lead's name.
recognised: {name} looks at you a moment too long. Then you see it on them: the mark, the same as the one you carry. Neither of you says anything about it for a while.

NT: You have it too. Good. I had begun to think I was the only one who woke up in a crater with a head full of nothing. I am working out what we were. Books first.
NF: I knew someone would come. I dreamed of falling, and of other people falling beside me. You were one of them, I think.
SJ: You fell too, didn't you? Then we are owed an explanation, and I mean to have it in order: what happened, who did it, and what is to be done about it.
SP: Another one off the same cart, then. Don't look so grim. We're alive, the ground's solid, and there's a fight somewhere near here. That's a start.

NT: {lead}. I have a theory about the Tower now. It is not finished. Neither are we.
NF: You came back. Most people don't. Sit a while, if you like.
SJ: {lead}. You keep turning up. Either we were meant to, or you are following me.
SP: {lead}! Still breathing. Good. I've been somewhere loud since I saw you last.

library.NT: There is a library at the edge of what I know. Something on its shelves has my handwriting in it. I am sure of that, and of nothing else.
library.NF: A library. I keep dreaming of a page I wrote and cannot read. If it is anywhere, it is there.
library.SJ: The library. If anybody wrote down what happened to us, it is on a shelf there, filed and waiting.
library.SP: A library, if you can believe it. Me. Somebody there owes me answers, and I'll take them in any order.

heading.tower: The Tower. I keep walking towards it without deciding to.
heading.keep: A keep. Walls, banners, people who think they are in charge. Somebody there knows something, or will fight me for not knowing.
heading.village: A village. People who cook. I would like to remember what it is to be ordinary.
heading.gate: A gate has opened. I can feel it from here, like a draught under a door. I'm going in.
heading.hut: Somewhere small and out of the way. I think better where nobody is looking at me.

lines.join_yes: Why not? Better a road with company than another crater on my own. Lead on, {lead}.
lines.join_not_yet: Not yet. I don't know you, and I don't yet know me. Find me again.
lines.join_full: There is no room in that company for one more, and I will not walk at the back of anyone's line.
lines.joined_note: {name} falls in with you, carrying the same mark you do.
lines.seen_note: {name}, {title}, is here. They carry the mark you share.
rumour: Travellers talk of {name}, {title}, seen lately at {place}. They say there is something odd about the eyes.
Somebody calling themselves {name} passed through {place}, asking questions nobody could answer.
Word from {place}: {name}, {title}, turned up there out of nowhere, like they'd fallen from the sky.
lines.rumour_road: {name}, {title}, was last seen on the road, heading for {place}.
